chunks: And from him (Al-Husayn ibn Idris) from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Khaliq who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Does the Muhrim (person in Ihram) seek shelter from the sun? He said: 'No, unless he is an old man or, as he said, one with an ailment.'
And if he seeks shelter from the harm of the sun or the rain, the redemption (Fida') is incumbent upon him, and likewise for the patient one.

What indicates this is what he narrated: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Ali ibn Muhammad who said: I wrote to him: Does the Muhrim cover himself if the sun or rain harms him, or if he is sick, or not? If he covers himself, is the redemption incumbent upon him or not? He wrote (peace be upon him): 'He covers himself and sheds blood, if God wills.'

key_terms.إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ: If God wills (a common phrase in juristic responses indicating divine permission or occurrence)
key_terms.الْفِدَاءُ: Redemption or compensation (usually sacrificing an animal) required for breaking a restriction
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.ذَا عِلَّةٍ: One with an ailment or excuse
key_terms.يَسْتَتِرُ: To seek shelter or cover oneself

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a Muhrim who covers themselves from the sun or rain during Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between voluntary covering and necessity-based sheltering for the Muhrim, a key nuance in Shia fiqh regarding the validity of Ihram restrictions. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms that while sheltering from sun or rain is permitted, it incurs the penalty of *Fida'* (blood sacrifice), aligning with the principle that minor violations of ritual state require expiation. The text highlights the scholarly consensus on the necessity of animal sacrifice as the primary form of redemption for such infractions during Hajj or Umrah.
